Visit note | 2025-12-10 12:30 PM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Gopal Bhattacharya, 49, male. Mr. Bhattacharya returns for review of his skin condition, mentioning that he has been scratching at night and finds his symptoms much worse in winter, accompanied by itchy dry patches on his elbows and knees. He works as a bus driver and relates that his skin issues started after working with cleaning chemicals in Old Dhaka. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus and uses emollient creams daily without relief from the itching alone. He denies skin bleeding or secondary infection signs. On examination: affected area about 4 cm across, BP 134/80 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 70 kg. The skin on the elbows and knees shows mild lichenification and dryness. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued for topical treatment. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-12-10 03:00 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Papiya Mitra, 68, female. Mrs. Mitra attends for follow-up regarding a burning sensation in both feet, numbness in her toes, and tingling like pins and needles. She is a retired civil servant and explains that these nerve symptoms started after years of high sugar found at a health camp in Mohammadpur. She has Essential hypertension alongside her neuropathy and reports taking her glucose-lowering therapy irregularly. She denies open foot sores or severe night cramps. On examination: reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 139/90 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 60 kg. Ankle jerks are diminished bilaterally. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-12-10 03:00 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Rabeya Sarkar, 25, female. Miss Sarkar presents for her first visit complaining of painful swallowing, a sore throat, and fever. She works as a fisherman and states her illness started after consuming cold drinks at a wedding in Kushtia. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus and notes feeling quite fatigued over the past two days. She denies shortness of breath or ear pain. On examination: temperature 102.7°F, BP 121/72 mmHg, pulse 96 bpm, weight 89 kg. Her throat shows erythematous and enlarged tonsils with small exudates. Assessment: Acute tonsillitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to gargle with warm salt water, eat soft food, and drink plenty of fluids. Follow-up in 1 week.
